cards.text: Hezekiah, king of Judah, just got the report: the Rabshakeh, an officer sent by the king of Assyria, came to Jerusalem and told the people not to trust the LORD to save them. So Hezekiah tears his clothes and puts on sackcloth.

cards.question: Clothes torn, sackcloth on. Where does King Hezekiah go?

answers.text: Into the house of the LORD

cards.text: Then he sends his top officials and the leading priests, all wearing sackcloth, to go see a prophet. No memo, no email: when it's THIS bad, you send the whole front office in person.

cards.question: Hezekiah sends Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe and the leading priests. Which prophet are they going to see?

cards.text: Hezekiah calls today "a day of distress, rebuke, and disgrace" and puts it this way: children have come to the point of birth, but there is no strength to deliver them. Friend, that's a man with nothing left in the tank.

cards.question: Hezekiah hopes the LORD heard the Rabshakeh defy the living God. He asks Isaiah to lift up a ___ for the remnant that still survives.

cards.text: Isaiah sends back the LORD's answer: don't be afraid of the words those Assyrian servants used to blaspheme Him. Then the LORD says He'll put a spirit in the king of Assyria so that he hears a rumor.

cards.question: Because of that rumor, the king of Assyria will go back to his own ___, and there the LORD will cause him to fall by the sword.

cards.text: The Rabshakeh finds his king fighting against Libnah, and Sennacherib, the king of Assyria, has been warned: Tirhakah king of Cush has set out to fight him. But I bet Jerusalem's still on his mind.

cards.question: True or false: Once Sennacherib hears Tirhakah is coming, he leaves Hezekiah alone.

cards.text: Round two. Sennacherib's new message lists kingdom after kingdom Assyria has already destroyed, like a man reading off his own trophy shelf.

cards.question: True or false: When Sennacherib asks if the gods of those nations rescued them, his point is that Hezekiah's God can't rescue Jerusalem either.

cards.text: Hezekiah reads the letter and goes up to the house of the LORD. Now me? I'd be up till 2 a.m. writing three angry replies I never send.

cards.question: What does Hezekiah do with Sennacherib's letter in the house of the LORD?

answers.text: Spreads it out before the LORD

cards.text: Hezekiah prays before the LORD. And before he asks for one single thing, he starts with who God is.

cards.question: What does Hezekiah say about the LORD at the start of his prayer?

answers.text: He alone is God over every kingdom
He is the greatest of all the gods
He is the God of Judah only

cards.text: He calls Him the One who made the heavens and the earth. Then he asks: "Incline Your ear, O LORD, and hear; open Your eyes, O LORD, and see."

cards.question: True or false: In his prayer, Hezekiah admits the kings of Assyria really have laid waste these nations and their lands.
Hezekiah says Assyria threw those nations' gods into the fire and destroyed them. Why could they?

answers.text: They were only wood and stone

cards.question: Hezekiah asks the LORD to save them from Sennacherib's hand. What reason does he give?

answers.text: So all kingdoms know the LORD alone is God
So Judah can finally rule over Assyria
So the people keep trusting their king

cards.text: Then Isaiah son of Amoz sends Hezekiah a message from the LORD: "I have heard your prayer concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria." And the LORD has a word for Sennacherib too, and friend, it is NOT a thank-you card.

cards.question: True or false: In the LORD's word against Sennacherib, the Daughter of Jerusalem trembles in fear of him.
Against whom has Sennacherib raised his voice and lifted his eyes in pride?

cards.text: The LORD quotes Sennacherib's own bragging back to him: chariots up the mountain peaks, Lebanon's tallest cedars cut down, Egypt's streams dried up under the soles of his feet. That's a man reading his own highlight reel OUT LOUD.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says Sennacherib's conquests happened apart from any plan of His.

cards.text: The LORD says the people of those cities were devoid of power, like grass on the rooftops, scorched before it is grown. And He knows Sennacherib's sitting down, his going out and coming in, and his raging against Him.

cards.question: Sennacherib's rage and arrogance have reached the LORD's ears. What does the LORD say He'll do with him?

answers.text: Put a hook in his nose and send him back
Let him take Jerusalem for a season
Give him one more year to turn around

cards.text: Then the LORD turns to Hezekiah and gives him a sign. This year and the next, they'll eat whatever grows on its own.

cards.question: In the LORD's sign, the first two years Judah eats whatever grows on its own. What about the third year?

answers.text: Assyria will come back for them
They'll have to leave the land

cards.text: Judah's surviving remnant will again take root below and bear fruit above, and the LORD says, "The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this." Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so take it from a leftover: what's left over is NOT finished.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says the king of Assyria will get at least one arrow into Jerusalem.

cards.text: No arrow, no shield, no siege ramp. The LORD says Sennacherib will go back the way he came, and he will not enter this city.

cards.question: The LORD says He'll defend Jerusalem and save it for His own sake and for the sake of His servant ___.

cards.text: And that very night, the angel of the LORD goes out to the camp of the Assyrians.

cards.question: What does the angel of the LORD do in the Assyrian camp that night?

answers.text: Sets all their tents on fire

cards.text: "When the people got up the next morning, there were all the dead bodies!" One night. That's all it took, friend.

cards.question: After that morning, Sennacherib breaks camp and withdraws. Where does he go?

cards.text: He stays put in Nineveh. Then one day, he's worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch.

cards.question: In the temple of Nisroch, Sennacherib is put to the sword by his own ___.

cards.text: His sons Adrammelech and Sharezer escape to the land of Ararat, and his son Esar-haddon reigns in his place. Don't close the oven yet, friend, because Hezekiah's story isn't finished.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the quoted verse, "One night." and "That's all it took, friend."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
